Another on 9 May, 2023
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice V.Gopala Krishna Rao
 M.A.C.M.A.No. 2274 of 2014
Judgement:
The appellant is 2nd respondent/Insurance company and the respondents are claim petitioner and
1st respondent in M.V.O.P.No.837 of 2008 on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims
Tribunal-cum-VI Additional District Judge, Kurnool.
The appellant filed the appeal questioning the legal validity of the order of the Tribunal.
2. For the sake of convenience, both the parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in the claim application.

3. The claim petitioner filed the petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- for the death of his wife K. Suvarna in a road accident that took place on 07.08.2007.
VGKR,J MACMA No.2274 of 2014 4.

The brief averments in the petition filed by the petitioner are as follows:
On 07.08.2007 the deceased along with others was proceeding to B. Thandrapadu village in an auto bearing registration No.AP 21X 5919 and when the auto reached near G.Pulla Reddy Engineering College, a lorry bearing registration No.AP 21T 4788 being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, came and dashed the auto.
Due to that, the deceased sustained injuries and died on the same day while undergoing treatment in the Government General Hospital, Kurnool.
The 1st respondent is owner and the 2nd respondent is insurer of the offending lorry.

Hence,
both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the claim petitioner.
5. The 1st respondent filed a counter by denying the manner of accident.
It is pleaded that while overtaking a bus, the auto hit the lorry and therefore, the driver of the auto is responsible for the accident and there is no fault on the part of the driver of the lorry.
VGKR,J 6.
The 2nd respondent/Insurance company also filed a counter by denying the manner of accident.

It is pleaded that the driver of the auto lost control over it and dashed the lorry of the 1st respondent and the driver of the 1st respondent had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the lorry as on The New India Assurance Company Ltd., vs K.Avulaiah Babu Another on 9 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127879999/
1 the date of the accident.

sentences.text: Therefore, the Insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation.

7. Based on the above pleadings of both the parties, the following issues were settled for trial by the Tribunal:
1) Whether the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry bearing No.AP 21T 4788?
2) Whether the 1st respondent violated the terms and conditions of the Insurance policy?
3) Whether the petitioner is entitled to any compensation from the respondents, and if so, to what extent?

4) To what relief?
8.
During the course of enquiry in the claim petition, on behalf of the petitioner, P.Ws.1 and 2 were examined and Exs.A.1 to A.10 VGKR,J were marked.
On behalf of the respondents, R.Ws.1 and 2 were examined and Exs.B.1 to B.6 were marked.

9. At the culmination of the enquiry, based on the material available on record, the Tribunal came to a conclusion that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending lorry and the 1st respondent violated the terms and conditions of the policy and accordingly, granted an amount of Rs.4,45,000/- with interest at 9% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit and directed the Insurance company to deposit the compensation to the claim petitioner in the first instance and then recover the same from the 1st respondent/owner of the offending lorry, by filing an execution petition, without filing any independent suit.
Aggrieved against the said order, the appellant/Insurance company preferred the present appeal.
10. Heard learned counsels for both the parties.

11. The appellant pleaded that the Tribunal failed to see that the driver of the offending lorry was not holding any valid driving licence VGKR,J and hence, the Insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and the Tribunal also erred in awarding interest at the rate of 9% p.a. which is exorbitant.

12. Now, the point for determination is:
Whether the order of the Tribunal needs any interference of this Court?
13. POINT: In order to prove the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending lorry, the petitioner relied on the evidence of P.Ws.1 and 2.
P.W.1 is not an eye witness to the accident.
P.W.2 is an eye witness to the accident.

He deposed that at the time of accident, he was travelling in the auto along with four persons including the driver and while they were travelling in the auto to the The New India Assurance Company Ltd., vs K.Avulaiah Babu

2 extreme left side of the road, the driver of the offending lorry dashed the auto, consequently, the deceased sustained multiple injuries and later died.
There is nothing in the cross-examination of P.W.2 to discredit his evidence and the suggestions put to him were also denied by him.
The petitioners also relied on Ex.A.1-certified copy of first information report, Ex.A.4-certified copy of charge sheet and VGKR,J Ex.A.7-certified copy of Motor Vehicle Inspector's report.
Ex . A.1 goes to show that first information report was registered against the driver of the offending lorry.
Ex.A.4 clearly goes to show that after completion of investigation, the Investigating Officer filed a charge sheet against the driver of the offending lorry.
Ex.A.7 discloses that the accident not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle.
The evidence of P.W.2 coupled with Exs.A.1, A.4 and A.7 clearly proves about the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending lorry resulting in the accident.
The learned Tribunal also, on appreciating the evidence on record, came to a conclusion that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending lorry.
Therefore, there is no need to interfere with the said finding given by the learned Tribunal.
14. According to the petitioner, the age of the deceased was 41 years at the time of accident, but no documentary evidence was filed in proof of the age of the deceased.
Hence, the age of the deceased was taken as 45 years by the Tribunal.
The multiplier applicable to the age group of the deceased is "14" as per the VGKR,J decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Varma case.

The Tribunal by giving cogent reasons fixed the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.5,000/- based on the material available on record and after deducting half of income towards personal expenses of the deceased,

arrived the loss of dependency to the family members of the deceased at Rs.4,20,000/- (Rs.2,500/-
x 12 months x multiplier "14").

Besides, the Tribunal awarded Rs.10,000/- towards loss of estate,
Rs.10,000/- towards loss of consortium and Rs.5,000/- towards funeral expenses.
In total, the Tribunal granted compensation of Rs.4,45,000/-.
Therefore, there is no need to interfere with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

15. The learned Tribunal in its order held that the 1st respondent insured the offending lorry with the 2nd respondent/Insurance company under Ex.B.2-copy of insurance policy and the policy was also in force as on the date of the accident and as the driver of the offending lorry had no valid driving licence at the time of accident, the Insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner and accordingly, ordered the 2nd respondent to pay the VGKR,J compensation to the petitioner in the first instance and later recover the same from the 1st respondent/owner of the offending lorry by filing an execution petition, without filing any independent suit.
This Court feels that there is no illegality in the said finding recorded by the learned Tribunal.

16. Insofar as awarding of interest @ 9% p.a. is concerned, this Court finds merit in the submission of the learned standing counsel for the appellant/Insurance company that the Tribunal awarded exorbitant rate of interest and therefore, the same has to be reduced from 9% p.a. to 7.5% p.a.
17.

Accordingly, the appeal is disposed of and the decree and order dated 16.07.2013 passed by the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-VI Additional District Judge, Kurnool, in M.V.O.P.No.837 of 2008 is modified by reducing the rate of interest from 9% p.a. to 7.5% p.a.
